name: Gurudongmar Lake
tagline: A sacred lake at about 5,430 m on the edge of the Tibetan plateau
summary: Gurudongmar is a glacial lake at about 5,430 m near the Tibet border, sacred to Buddhists and linked to Guru Padmasambhava. It is a dawn day trip from Lachen, 67 km away, open only to Indian citizens. Go April to June or October to November and take the altitude seriously.
meta_description: Gurudongmar Lake at 5,430 m: permits (Indians only), the dawn drive from Lachen, altitude safety, best months, costs and road status after the 2023 flood.
intro: Gurudongmar is one of the highest lakes in India that tourists can reach by road. It lies at about 5,430 m on a bare, windswept plateau north of Thangu, close to the border with Tibet, with the snow peaks of the Kangchengyao range behind. In winter it freezes over; from May the ice breaks up and the water turns a deep blue.

The lake is sacred to Buddhists, who link it with Guru Padmasambhava, and it is also visited by Sikhs. A small shrine stands by the shore with prayer flags. Treat the place with respect: do not throw coins or rubbish into the water, and keep your voice down.

Getting here is a serious undertaking. You sleep in Lachen, leave around 4 am and drive 67 km through army checkposts, reaching the lake by about 7–8 am. At this height the air holds roughly half the oxygen of sea level. Most visitors spend 30–45 minutes, walk slowly and drive straight back down.

highlights.title: One of India's highest lakes
highlights.text: At about 5,430 m the lake sits higher than any other place most travellers will ever reach by road.

highlights.title: The Guru Rinpoche legend
highlights.text: Local tradition says Guru Padmasambhava blessed part of the lake so it would not freeze, giving herders water in winter.

highlights.title: The plateau landscape
highlights.text: Beyond Thangu the trees end and the land opens into brown, high desert under snow peaks, close to Tibet.

highlights.title: Blue water in autumn
highlights.text: From October to early November the lake is usually clear, still and deep blue in the morning light.

facts: Indian citizens only, via registered operator; foreigners not allowed

how_to_reach.text: All visits are in the registered vehicle on your Lachen package. Drivers leave Lachen around 4 am and pass army checkposts at Thangu and beyond. Private self-drive is not allowed.
On a shared group tour the Gurudongmar run is included and the jeep is shared with other guests. Everyone leaves and returns together.
Fly to Bagdogra, drive to Gangtok, then to Lachen the next day. The lake is reached on the third morning at the earliest.

where_to_stay: There are no stays at the lake. Sleep in Lachen at about 2,750 m, where lodges and homestays cost ₹1,500–3,000 a room with meals and better hotels ₹3,500–7,000. Two nights in Lachen before the lake is safer than one.
tips: Do not go if you already have altitude symptoms in Lachen.
Walk slowly at the lake, do not run or climb the slopes, and keep your stay short.
Carry water, sunglasses, sunscreen, a warm cap and windproof gloves; the wind is hard and the sun strong.
Talk to your doctor before the trip if you have heart, lung or blood pressure problems, or if you are pregnant.
Ask the operator the day before whether the road is open; snow and landslides close it often.

local_word.meaning: Lake; many high lakes in Sikkim carry it in their names

story.title: The lake that Guru Rinpoche kept from freezing
paras: Gurudongmar takes its name from Guru Padmasambhava, the teacher who is said to have brought Buddhism to Tibet and Sikkim in the 8th century. Buddhists in Sikkim call him Guru Rinpoche, and many places in the state are linked to his travels.

The story most often told is that herders who lived on this cold plateau had no water in winter, because the lake froze solid. They asked the Guru for help, and he touched part of the lake, so that a section of it would stay unfrozen even in the coldest months. Pilgrims still regard the water as blessed and some carry a little home.

The lake is also revered by Sikhs, some of whom link it with a visit by Guru Nanak. The question of who should keep a shrine at the lake later became a dispute that reached the courts, and today the shore has a small Buddhist shrine. Whatever your faith, the lake is treated as holy ground, so behave as you would in a temple.

faqs.q: Can foreigners visit Gurudongmar Lake?
faqs.a: No. Gurudongmar Lake is closed to foreign nationals. Foreigners with a Protected Area Permit can go to Lachen and the Lachung side up to Yumthang, but not to Gurudongmar or Zero Point. Indian citizens can visit with a permit arranged by a registered tour operator. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How high is Gurudongmar Lake?
faqs.a: About 5,430 m, though some sources give slightly different figures. That is higher than Everest Base Camp in Nepal, and roughly 2,700 m above Lachen, where you sleep the night before. It is one of the highest lakes in the world reachable by road.

faqs.q: Is Gurudongmar safe for children?
faqs.a: Operators and doctors generally advise against taking babies and young children to 5,430 m, because they cannot always tell you how they feel. Healthy older children can go if they are well in Lachen, with a short stay at the lake. When in doubt, a parent and child can wait at Thangu or Lachen.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Gurudongmar?
faqs.a: April to June, when the ice is breaking up, and October to early November, when the sky is clearest and the water blue. From December to March the lake is frozen and the road often closes after snow. June to September brings monsoon landslides on the way.

faqs.q: How long can I stay at the lake?
faqs.a: Most people stay 30–45 minutes, which is enough to walk to the shore, visit the shrine and take pictures. Staying longer raises the risk of altitude sickness, and the wind strengthens through the morning. The army may also ask vehicles to head back by a set time.

faqs.q: What are the signs of altitude sickness at Gurudongmar?
faqs.a: Headache, nausea, dizziness, unusual tiredness and breathlessness at rest. Confusion, stumbling or a wet cough are danger signs that need immediate descent. If anyone shows these, go down at once. Oxygen from a can can help briefly, but descent is the real treatment.

faqs.q: Does Gurudongmar Lake freeze?
faqs.a: Yes, the lake freezes over in winter, usually from about December to April. Local tradition holds that part of the lake, blessed by Guru Padmasambhava, does not freeze completely. From May the ice breaks up, and by October the lake is open water.

faqs.q: How cold is it at Gurudongmar?
faqs.a: Even in May and October, early mornings are below freezing and the wind makes it feel much colder. In winter temperatures fall far below zero. Wear thermals, a down or heavy jacket, a windproof layer, a woollen cap and gloves, and protect your eyes from glare.

faqs.q: Is the Gurudongmar road open after the 2023 flood?
faqs.a: The flood of October 2023 and later landslides damaged roads around Chungthang and the Lachen valley, and tourist access to Lachen and Gurudongmar was suspended for long periods. It reopens when repairs and army clearance allow. Ask your operator before booking. Check current status before you travel.

experiences.title: Morning at Gurudongmar Lake
experiences.summary: A short, careful visit to the lake shore in the early morning, when the water is still and the peaks are clear.
body: Vehicles reach a parking area above the lake and you walk down a short slope to the shore. The water is blue or frozen depending on the month, with the Kangchengyao massif behind. Prayer flags and a small shrine stand by the edge.

Walk slowly, even downhill, because climbing back up is harder than it looks. Take your pictures, spend a few quiet minutes and head back while you still feel well. Do not throw anything into the lake.
experiences.best_time: 7–9 am, from April to June and October to early November.

faqs.q: Is there a fee at the lake?
faqs.a: There is no separate fee at the lake for Indian visitors on a permitted package. The permit and vehicle are covered by your operator. Carry your original ID for the army checks on the way.

faqs.q: Are there toilets or shops at the lake?
faqs.a: Facilities are very limited, and depending on the season there may be none at the lake. Use the toilets at Thangu on the way up. Carry water and a snack.

faqs.q: Can I walk around the lake?
faqs.a: No. Stay near the viewing area and the shrine. Walking further is tiring at this height and parts of the area are restricted by the army.

experiences.title: The lakeside shrine at Gurudongmar
experiences.summary: A small shrine and prayer flags by the shore mark the lake as holy ground linked with Guru Padmasambhava.
body: Pilgrims light butter lamps or incense, tie prayer flags and offer khadas, the white scarves of greeting. Some collect a little water from the lake to take home. The shrine is simple, and its peace is part of the visit.
Remove your hat inside, keep your voice down and do not touch religious objects. Walk clockwise when circling. If you bring a khada or prayer flag, buy it in Gangtok or Lachen beforehand.
experiences.best_time: Early morning, when the wind is lightest.

faqs.q: Which faiths consider Gurudongmar sacred?
faqs.a: Buddhists revere it for its link with Guru Padmasambhava, and Sikhs also hold it sacred through a tradition linking it with Guru Nanak. Hindus and others visit too. Everyone is welcome if they behave respectfully.

faqs.q: Can I take water from the lake?
faqs.a: Many pilgrims collect a small bottle of water. Do not wash, swim or throw anything into the lake. Take your empty bottles away with you.

faqs.q: Should I bring an offering?
faqs.a: It is not required. If you wish, bring a khada or prayer flags from Gangtok or Lachen. Do not leave plastic or food at the shrine.

experiences.title: The plateau drive from Thangu to Gurudongmar
experiences.summary: Above Thangu the road leaves the trees and crosses a high, bare plateau close to Tibet, one of the most unusual landscapes in India.
body: From Thangu at about 3,900 m the road climbs past army camps into open country of brown hills, gravel flats and snow peaks. In good light the colours change from purple to gold. You may see yaks, and occasionally wild animals at a distance.
Photography of army installations is forbidden; your driver will tell you where you can stop. Keep window stops short, stay warm and keep drinking water.
experiences.best_time: Dawn on the way up, mid-morning on the way down.

faqs.q: Can I photograph along the plateau road?
faqs.a: Landscape photography is generally fine at stops your driver chooses. Photographing army camps, vehicles, bridges or soldiers is not allowed and can lead to problems. When in doubt, ask the driver.

faqs.q: Is the road rough?
faqs.a: Parts are rough, with gravel, stream crossings and patches of snow or ice. SUVs with experienced local drivers handle it every day. People prone to motion sickness should eat lightly and sit in front.

faqs.q: Will I see wildlife on the way?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Yaks are common, and lucky travellers spot animals such as blue sheep at a distance. Do not leave the vehicle to chase sightings; the driver must keep to time and permitted stops.

experiences.title: Staying safe at 5,430 m
experiences.summary: A simple plan for the altitude at Gurudongmar: sleep low, go up early, stay briefly, and come down at the first serious symptom.
body: The safest plan is two nights in Lachen or Lachung before the lake, plenty of water, no alcohol and a light dinner. Some doctors prescribe acetazolamide for travellers to high altitude; only take it on medical advice. Carry a small oxygen can, but treat it as a short help, not a cure.

At the lake, walk slowly, do not run, and keep the visit to 30–45 minutes. If anyone develops a worsening headache, vomiting, confusion or breathlessness at rest, drive down at once. Children, pregnant women and people with heart or lung disease should take medical advice before going.
experiences.best_time: Prepare from the night in Lachen.

faqs.q: Should I take medicine for altitude?
faqs.a: Only on a doctor's advice. Acetazolamide is commonly prescribed to help prevent altitude sickness, but it is not right for everyone and has side effects. Discuss it with your doctor before you leave home.

faqs.q: Do drivers carry oxygen?
faqs.a: Many do, and you can buy portable oxygen cans in Gangtok or Lachen. Oxygen gives short relief but does not replace descent. If symptoms are serious, go down immediately.

faqs.q: Can I go to Gurudongmar after only one night in Lachen?
faqs.a: Most packages do exactly that, and most healthy adults manage. A second night lowers the risk. If you felt unwell in Lachen, skip the lake rather than force it.
